source_text: Ἀλλ᾿ οἱ πονεῖν ἕτοιμοι ἐπὶ τοῖς καλλίστοις οὐ πρότερον ἀποστήσονται ζητοῦντες τὴν ἀλήθειαν πρὶν ἂν τὴν ἀπόδειξιν ἀπ᾿ αὐτῶν λάβωσι τῶν γραφῶν. ἔστι μὲν οὖν κοινά τινα τῶν ἀνθρώπων κριτήρια καθάπερ τὰ αἰσθητήρια. τὰ δ᾿ ἄλλα τῶν βουληθέντων καὶ ἀσκησάντων τὰ ἀληθῆ. τὰ διὰ νοῦ καὶ λογισμοῦ τεχνικὰ λόγων ἀληθῶν τε καὶ ψευδῶν. μέγιστον δὲ τὸ καὶ τὴν οἴησιν ἀποθέσθαι. ἐν μέσῳ καταστάντας ἀκριβοῦς ἐπιστήμης καὶ προπετοῦς δοξοσοφίας, καὶ γνῶναι ὅτι ὁ τὴν αἰώνιον ἐλπίζων ἀνάπαυσιν γιγνώσκει καὶ τὴν εἴσοδον αὐτῆς ἐπίπονον οὖσαν καὶ »τεθλιμμένην«. ὁ δὲ ἅπαξ εὐαγγελισθεὶς καὶ »τὸ σωτήριόν« φησιν »ἰδών«, ἐν ᾗ ὥρᾳ ἂν ἐπιγνῷ, μὴ »ἐπιστρεφέσθω εἰς τὰ ὀπίσω καθάπερ ἡ Αὼτ γυνὴ« μηδὲ εἰς τὸν πρότερον βίον τὸν τοῖς αἰσθητοῖς προσανέχοντα, μηδὲ μὴν εἰς τὰς αἱρέσεις παλινδρομείτω· ἐρίζουσι γὰρ ἁμῇ γέ πῃ, τὸν ὄντα μὴ γινώσκουσαι θεόν. »ὁ γὰρ φιλῶν πατέρα ἢ μητέρα ὑπὲρ ἐμέ«, τὸν ὄντως πατέρα καὶ διδάσκαλον τῆς ἀληθείας, τὸν ἀναγεννῶντα καὶ ἀνακτίζοντα καὶ τιθηνούμενον τὴν ψυχὴν τὴν ἐξειλεγμένην, »οὐκ ἔστι μου ἄξιος«, ἄξιος λέγει τοῦ εἶναι υἱὸς θεοῦ καὶ μαθητὴς θεοῦ ὁμοῦ καὶ φίλος καὶ συγγενής. »οὐδεὶς γὰρ εἰς τὰ ὀπίσω βλέπων καὶ ἐπιβάλλων τὴν χεῖρα αὐτοῦ ἐπ᾿ ἄροτρον εὔθετος τῇ βασιλείᾳ τοῦ θεοῦ.« Ἀλλ᾿. ὡς ἔοικεν. τοῖς πολλοῖς καὶ μέχρι νῦν δοκεῖ ἡ Μαριὰμ λεχὼ εἶναι διὰ τὴν τοῦ παιδίου γέννησιν, οὐκ οὖσα λεχώ (καὶ γὰρ μετὰ τὸ τεκεῖν αὐτὴν μαιωθεῖσάν φασί τινες παρθένον εὑρεθῆναι)· τοιαῦται δ᾿ ἡμῖν αἱ κυριακαὶ γραφαί, τὴν ἀλήθειαν ἀποτίκτουσαι καὶ μένουσαι παρθένοι μετὰ τῆς ἐπικρύψεως τῶν τῆς ἀληθείας μυστηρίων. »τέτοκεν καὶ οὐ τέτοκεν«, φησὶν ἡ γραφή, ὡς ἂν ἐξ αὑτῆς. οὐκ ἐκ συνδυασμοῦ συλλαβοῦσα. διόπερ τοῖς γνωστικοῖς κεκυήκασιν αἱ γραφαί, αἱ δὲ αἱρέσεις οὐκ ἐκμαθοῦσαι ὡς μὴ κεκυηκυίας παραπέμπονται. πάντων δὲ ἀνθρώπων τὴν αὐτὴν κρίσιν ἐχόντων οἱ μὲν ἀκολουθοῦντες τῷ αἱροῦντι λόγῳ ποιοῦνται τὰς πίστεις, οἱ δὲ ἡδοναῖς σφᾶς αὐτοὺς ἐκδεδωκότες βιάζονται πρὸς τὰς ἐπιθυμίας τὴν γραφήν. δεῖ δ᾿, οἶμαι, τῷ τῆς ἀληθείας ἐραστῇ ψυχικῆς εὐτονίας· σφάλλεσθαι γὰρ ἀνάγκη μέγιστα τοὺς μεγίστοις ἐγχειροῦντας πράγμασιν, ἢν μὴ τὸν κανόνα τῆς ἀληθείας παρ᾿ αὐτῆς λαβόντες ἔχωσι τῆς ἀληθείας. οἱ τοιοῦτοι δέ, ἅτε ἀποπεσόντες τῆς ὀρθῆς ὁδοῦ. κἀν τοῖς πλείστοις τῶν κατὰ μέρος σφάλλονται εἰκότως. διὰ τὸ μὴ ἔχειν ἀληθῶν καὶ ψευδῶν κριτήριον συγγεγυμνασμένον ἀκριβῶς τὰ δέοντα αἱρεῖσθαι. εἰ γὰρ ἐκέκτηντο, ταῖς θείαις ἐπείθοντο ἂν γραφαῖς.
pass_a_gloss: But those ready to labor for the best things will not stop seeking the truth before they receive proof from the scriptures. There are indeed some common criteria of men, like the senses. But for those who have willed and practiced the truth, there are technical words of truth and falsehood through mind and reasoning. The greatest thing is to lay aside opinion. Having stood in the middle of precise knowledge and forward doctrine, and to know that the one hoping for eternal rest also knows the entrance to it is laborious and 'narrow'. But the one who has been evangelized once and says 'I have seen the salvation', in whatever hour he recognizes, let him not turn back to the things behind like the woman Lot, nor to the former life which yields to the senses, nor let him waver to the heresies; for they contend in a way, not knowing the existing God. 'For the one loving father or mother more than me', the truly father and teacher of truth, the one regenerating and acquiring and nourishing the chosen soul, 'is not worthy of me', he says, worthy of being son of God and disciple of God, and friend and relative. 'For no one looking back and putting his hand on the plow is fit for the kingdom of God'. But, as it seems, to many even now the Mary who gave birth appears to be a woman who has given birth because of the birth of the child, not being a woman who has given birth (for some say that after she gave birth, she was found a virgin); such are the Lord's scriptures to us, producing the truth and remaining virgins after the covering of the mysteries of truth. 'She has given birth and has not given birth', the scripture says, as if from itself, not having conceived from a union. Therefore, the scriptures have been impregnated with the truth for the knowledgeable, but the heresies, not having learned as if not having been impregnated, are sent away. All men having the same judgment, some follow the choosing word and make their beliefs, but others, having given themselves over to pleasures, force the scripture to their desires. But, I think, the lover of truth needs psychic strength; for it is necessary for those attempting the greatest matters to fail greatly, unless they have the standard of truth, having taken it from truth itself. Such people, having fallen away from the right path, fail in most of the partial things, reasonably, because they do not have a criterion of true and false things, trained precisely to choose the necessary things. For if they had it, they would obey the divine scriptures.

pass_b_english: Those who are prepared to labor for the highest goods will not cease seeking the truth until they receive proof of it from the Scriptures. There are indeed certain criteria common to all people, such as the senses. But for those who have willed the truth and disciplined themselves in it, there are technical terms for truth and falsehood that operate through the mind and reasoning. The greatest step is to lay aside mere opinion. Taking a stand between precise knowledge and reckless pseudo-wisdom, one must recognize that the person who hopes for eternal rest also knows that the entrance to it is laborious and "narrow." The one who has once been evangelized and declares, "I have seen the salvation" (Luke 2:30), must not turn back to the things behind, like Lot's wife, at whatever hour he comes to recognize it; nor must he return to the former life that yields to the senses, nor waver back into heresies. For the heresies contend in some fashion, not knowing the God who truly exists. "Whoever loves father or mother more than me" (Matthew 10:37) — meaning the true Father and Teacher of truth, the one who regenerates, rebuilds, and nurtures the chosen soul — "is not worthy of me." Jesus says such a person is not worthy of being a son of God and a disciple of God, both friend and kinsman. "No one who puts a hand to the plow and looks back is fit for the kingdom of God" (Luke 9:62).

Yet, as it appears, to many even now Mary seems to be a woman who has given birth because of the child's birth, though she is not a woman who has given birth in the ordinary sense (for some say that after she bore him she was found to be a virgin still). Such are the Lord's Scriptures to us: they give birth to the truth yet remain virgins after the veiling of the mysteries of truth. "She has given birth and has not given birth," the Scripture says, as if from itself — not having conceived through sexual union. Therefore the Scriptures have been impregnated with truth for the Gnostics (the knowing ones), but the heresies, having not learned as if not having been impregnated, are sent away. All people possess the same faculty of judgment; some follow the choosing Word and form their convictions accordingly, while others, having surrendered themselves to pleasures, force Scripture to conform to their desires. But, I think, the lover of truth requires psychic strength; for those who attempt the greatest matters are bound to fail greatly unless they possess the standard of truth, having received it from truth itself. Such people, having fallen from the right path, rightly fail in most particulars, because they lack a criterion of true and false that has been rigorously trained to choose what is necessary. For if they possessed it, they would obey the divine Scriptures.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the nuances of the Greek text. Pass A provides a faithful literal rendering, and Pass B provides a more fluent version that correctly identifies the scriptural allusions (Luke 2:30, Matthew 10:37, Luke 9:62) which were present in the Greek text as quotes/allusions. The distinction between 'knowledge' and 'pseudo-wisdom' (δοξοσοφίας) is preserved. The complex section regarding the Virgin Mary and the 'impregnated' scriptures is handled correctly in both versions.
